text: China, officially the People's Republic of China (PRC), is a country in East Asia. It is divided into 33 province-level divisions, including two special administrative regions. Beijing is the capital, while Shanghai is the most populous city by urban area. Its geography features the Central Plain, major rivers such as the Yangtze and Yellow River, deserts, subtropical and temperate forests, plateaus, and mountain ranges such as the Himalayas. It is the world's second-most populous country after India, with a population exceeding 1.4 billion (17% of the world's population). Covering 9.6 million square kilometers (3,700,000 sq mi), it is the third largest country by area. Humans first arrived in China during the Paleolithic. During the 2nd millennium BCE, dynastic states emerged. In 221 BCE, China was unified under the Qin, followed by the Han dynasty, ushering in two millennia of imperial rule across periods of unity and division.
title: China

text: The imperial era saw the expansion of the Silk Road and the invention of gunpowder, paper, printing, and the compass. After increased Western political, economic, and philosophical influence, the empire was succeeded by the Republic of China (ROC) after the 1911 Revolution. The Warlord Era and Chinese Civil War followed, interrupted by the Second Sino-Japanese War, which ended in a Chinese victory. In 1949, the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) proclaimed the PRC and the ROC retreated to Taiwan. Both sides still claim political legitimacy. CCP attempts to advance its political program faltered through famine and political turmoil. The reform and opening-up that began in 1978 moved China towards a socialist market economy, spurring economic growth. China is a unitary state with the CCP as its sole ruling party. It is one of the five permanent members of the UN Security Council and a member of many multilateral organizations.
title: China

text: China is the world's largest manufacturer and has the second-largest economy by nominal GDP. International organizations have criticized China, alleging authoritarianism and human rights abuses. Possessing a large military, space program, and nuclear stockpile, China has been described as a superpower due to its influence in geopolitics, science and technology, manufacturing, economics, and culture. Chinese art and culture have influenced much of Asia, with a literary tradition dating back millennia to the Chinese classics. China is the birthplace of Confucianism and Daoism, which form the traditional three teachings of Chinese philosophy and folk religion alongside Buddhism. Chinese cuisine is diverse and highly regional, with rice as a staple in the south and wheat in the north. It has 60 World Heritage Sites, including the Great Wall and Grand Canal.
title: China

text: The Han, speakers of Sinitic languages, are China's dominant ethnicity, although it is home to 55 recognized minorities, including the Hui, Mongols, Tibetans, Uyghurs, and Zhuang.
title: China

text: The word "China" has been used in English since the 16th century; however, it was not used by the Chinese themselves during this period. Its origin has been traced through Portuguese, Malay, and Persian back to the Sanskrit word Cīna (चिन), used in ancient India. Cīna was first used in early Hindu scriptures dating from the 3rd century BCE to 4th century CE, including the Mahabharata and the Laws of Manu. In 1655, the missionary Martino Martini suggested that the word China is derived ultimately from the ancient state of Qin. This remains a common etymology. Another possible source is the ancient Guizhou polity of Yelang, known as ʐina in Loloish languages. The official name of the modern state is the "People's Republic of China" (中华人民共和国; Zhōnghuá Rénmín Gònghéguó). The shorter form of this name is 中国; Zhōngguó, from zhōng ('central' or 'middle') and guó ('state'), a term first used for the demesne of the Western Zhou dynasty.
title: China

text: The names of ruling imperial dynasties were typically used to refer to the state and its territories. In the 1800s, Zhongguo was officially adopted as the name of the country by the Qing dynasty.
title: China

text: Evidence of early humans such as Homo erectus in China dates to the Paleolithic, around 1.7 million years ago, with unconfirmed sites as old as 2 million years ago. Modern Homo sapiens are attested from around 50,000 years ago. Following the end of the Last Glacial Period, in about 8,000 BCE, pottery-making Neolithic cultures emerged. By the 6000s BCE, sedentary agricultural societies had spread across the lower Yellow River basin. These societies became increasingly complex, urbanized, and stratified, but many experienced a population collapse in the late 2000s BCE for unclear reasons.
title: China

text: After 2000 BCE, a Bronze Age culture emerged in the Central Plain, dubbed the Erlitou culture after its main site. Erlitou has been controversially identified with the Xia, the traditionally-accepted first dynasty, but no written records exist to confirm this. The Shang dynasty purportedly succeeded the Xia around 1600 BCE, with its early stages tentatively identified with an expansionist state known archaeologically as the Erligang culture. The historicity of the Late Shang is attested through divinational writings in the oracle bone script. These are the earliest known form of writing in China and the ancestor of modern Chinese characters. The Shang were overthrown by the Zhou c. 1046 BCE. The Zhou ruled over a vast and loose confederation of vassal states across central China, which was gradually weakened by regional lords. Centralized authority collapsed in 771 BCE, giving way to constant regional warfare.
title: China

text: During the Eastern Zhou, the multitude of small polities of the Spring and Autumn period evolved into seven territorial Warring States. Literary and philosophical developments of this period include the emergence of various schools of thought, such as Confucianism, Daoism, Mohism, and Legalism, alongside Chinese classics like the Confucian Analects and the Daoist Dao De Jing.
title: China

text: In the 220s BCE, Qin rapidly conquered the other warring states. In 221, its ruler Qin Shi Huang proclaimed himself the first emperor (皇帝; Huángdì) and founded the Qin dynasty. He led an autocratic Legalist state organized in a system of commanderies and counties. The dynasty lasted only fifteen years, falling soon after his death from revolts and civil war. After the collapse, the Han dynasty emerged to rule China between 206 BCE and 220 CE. The Han gradually reinstated centralized control, legitimizing their rule through Confucian scholarship and political institutions which would be maintained in some form into the 20th century. Military expeditions against the Xiongnu, a confederation of nomadic steppe tribes, expanded Han influence into parts of Central Asia and helped to establish the Silk Road, allowing for trade connections between China and western Eurasia. Contemporaneously, merchants established maritime trade routes linking China, Southeast Asia, and India.
title: China

text: The dynasty is the namesake of the Han Chinese, China's main ethnic group. The Han faced widespread uprisings and the emergence of local warlords in the 100s and 200s CE. By 220, the empire was split into the Three Kingdoms. These were briefly united by the Jin dynasty in 280, which fell into civil war. Sinicized formerly-nomadic peoples who had settled in Northern China, such as the Xiongnu, rebelled and founded new dynasties. Various Han Chinese dynasties in Southern China emerged in the 300s. During these conflicts, Buddhism was introduced to China via the Silk Road.
title: China

text: The Song dynasty rose to power in 960. It faced military crises, unable to subdue its Sinicized non-Han neighbors, the Khitan-led Liao dynasty and the Tangut-led Western Xia. The Song's consistent focus on defense resulted in a heavily centralized state and military, which made the first military application of gunpowder. Books became widely available by the proliferation of printing technology, while the elite class of scholar-officials grew increasingly powerful. Production, population, and trade expanded massively, alongside innovations such as industrial metallurgy and hydraulic machinery. The Song capital Kaifeng was overrun by the Jurchen-led Jin in 1127, forcing the Song to retreat to Southern China. During this period, the revivalist philosophical movement of Neo-Confucianism emerged.
title: China

text: In 1206, Genghis Khan united the nomadic Mongols to the north under the Mongol Empire. Over the following fifty years, they conquered the Western Xia and the Jin, in addition to their other conquests as far west as Europe. The empire split into separate khanates, with Mongol leader Kublai Khan establishing the Yuan dynasty and subjugating the Song in the 1270s. Although Chinese culture remained largely unchanged, the Yuan maintained a Mongol elite culture and established a complex ethnic and occupational hierarchy. Foreign presence increased as China became more connected to Eurasian trade routes. In the 1340s, central China was devastated by disease, famine, and severe flooding along the Yellow River. Various rebellions erupted, leading to a peasant leader establishing the Ming dynasty in 1368 and declaring himself the Hongwu Emperor. The Ming later moved their capital from Nanjing to Beijing, with the Forbidden City as the imperial palace.
title: China

text: However, the lower Yangtze remained the wealthiest region. Trade grew, and the European colonization of the Americas brought new crops and a massive influx of silver to China. The population doubled, and a growing publishing industry began producing works in vernacular Chinese, including the Four Classic Novels. The Ming state declined, and by the 1600s, became unable to contain peasant rebellions. The Manchus to the north declared the Qing dynasty in 1636 and conquered the Ming, killing their last claimant emperor in 1662 and conquering a Ming rump state on Taiwan in 1683. From the late 1600s to the end of the 1700s, the High Qing era saw economic growth and territorial expansion westward, including the conquest of Tibet and much of Central Asia.
title: China

text: European powers fought various wars against the Qing dynasty during the 19th century. These began with the United Kingdom's First Opium War in 1839–1842, which resulted in the first of the "unequal treaties" imposed on the dynasty. These opened treaty ports, allowed Christian missionary activity, and loosened trade restrictions. China faced an economic crisis and internal unrest, and uprisings such as the 1850–1864 Taiping Rebellion resulted in the deaths of millions. Reformist factions of the Qing responded with the Self-Strengthening Movement, seeking to adopt Western weapons and technologies, but this had a limited impact for much of the empire. The Empire of Japan's defeat of the Qing in the First Sino-Japanese War (1894–1895) resulted in the loss of Taiwan and the growth of both reformist and revolutionary political movements.
title: China

text: An imperial push for reform in 1898 ended after an internal coup, while the anti-foreign Boxer Rebellion was defeated by a coalition of foreign powers in 1901. The late Qing dynasty again advanced reforms, but growing revolutionary and anti-Manchu sentiment culminated in the 1911 Revolution. A coalition of revolutionaries led by Sun Yat-sen overthrew the Qing and declared the Republic of China (ROC) in 1912.
title: China

text: After a string of military victories, CCP chairman Mao Zedong formally proclaimed the People's Republic of China (PRC) in 1949. The ROC government retreated to Taiwan and continued to claim legitimacy. The following year, the PRC occupied and annexed Tibet. The PRC, which the CCP described as a "people's democratic dictatorship", enacted many reforms: it restructured the economy under state control, promoted literacy and gender equality, and expanded heavy industry. The Land Reform Movement, in which the state encouraged and organized peasant violence against landlords, leading to the death of upwards of a million people, had begun in northern China during the civil war and extended to most of the rest of China between 1950 and 1952. It distributed landlord land to the peasants as private property, but it was soon followed by collectivization of the land.
title: China

text: In 1958, Mao launched the Great Leap Forward, a mass industrialization project which resulted in the Great Chinese Famine and millions of deaths. As the Cold War deepened, China grew politically isolated from its former ally, the Soviet Union, as well as the Western Bloc. It detonated its first atomic bomb in 1964. Attempting to reassert control over the CCP after the Great Leap, Mao and his allies launched the Cultural Revolution in 1966, sparking a decade of political violence, crackdowns on perceived counterrevolutionaries, and social upheaval that lasted until Mao's death in 1976. Deng Xiaoping served as paramount leader from 1978 to 1989. The reform and opening-up policies of the 1980s and 1990s saw economic liberalization towards a socialist market economy, rapid economic growth, and improved relations with the West. Political dissent culminated in a mild crackdown early in 1987 and a much more severe and prolonged crackdown in 1989 that included the Tiananmen Square massacre.
title: China

text: China shifted away from an agricultural economy and rapidly urbanized, although this led to stark economic inequality between urban and rural areas, as well as environmental deterioration. Since the 1990s, market forces have become China's main economic driver. Under the general secretaryship of Xi Jinping since 2012, he has launched a far-reaching anti-corruption campaign, expanded Chinese economic influence through the Belt and Road Initiative, and abolished term limits for himself as state president.
title: China

text: China's geography is highly varied, featuring a dry and mountainous west, alongside both mountains and wide river valleys in the east. Chinese civilization was traditionally centered in the lowlands around China's two longest rivers: the Yangtze and the Yellow River, both originating on the Tibetan Plateau. This temperate region is bordered by forest and steppe to the north, as well as the mountainous and subtropical south. China's shoreline spans the Bohai Sea, Yellow Sea, East China Sea, and South China Sea, all part of the Pacific Ocean. Its largest island is Taiwan, and the largest governed by the PRC is Hainan. Poyang Lake is the largest of the country's many freshwater lakes. Large mountain ranges in the west, including the Himalayas and Tian Shan, separate China from South and Central Asia. China features both the Turpan Depression, among the deepest points on land, and the high Tibetan Plateau.
title: China

text: The world's highest point, Mount Everest (8,848 metres or 29,029 feet above sea level), lies on the border with Nepal. China has a wide variety of ore and mineral resources. China's climate is dominated by dry seasons and wet monsoons, which lead to pronounced seasonal temperature differences. In the winter, northern winds coming from high-latitude areas are cold and dry; in summer, southern winds from coastal areas at lower latitudes are warm and moist. The northwestern deserts receive as little as 50 mm (2.0 in) of rainfall annually, while much of southern China exceeds 1,000 mm (39 in). Eastern China is well-suited for agriculture, with two or three harvests per year. The south is dominated by rice farming, while the north grows crops such as wheat and maize. China frequently faces natural disasters. Its adjacency to both the Pacific Ring of Fire and the Alpide belt (tectonic belts) results in frequent earthquakes, the cause of the majority of China's natural disaster deaths.
title: China

text: Severe quakes such as the 1976 Tangshan earthquake cause hundreds of thousands of deaths. Rainstorms and flooding are common hazards, with the Yellow River's perennial floods devastating the surrounding plains throughout recorded history. Typhoons frequently impact southeastern China.
title: China

text: China is one of 17 megadiverse countries, containing a wide variety of forests, shrublands, wetlands, steppes, and deserts, which host (as of 2018) 92,300 known species and subspecies of plants, animals, and fungi. According to government surveys, China's forest coverage grew from 10% of the overall territory in 1949 to 25% in 2024. The far north contains taiga, which transitions into deciduous forest to the south. South of the Yangtze, mixed conifer and deciduous forest is common, with tropical and subtropical forests farther south. In the 21st century, China has suffered from environmental deterioration and pollution due to rapid development, alongside the broader effects of climate change. About 11% of its plant species and 21% of its vertebrate species are threatened or endangered due to habitat loss, pollution, and poaching. "Flagship" endangered species such as the giant panda and tiger have received additional funding and protection.
title: China

text: Although China has the world's highest CO2 emissions, it only emits 8 tons of CO2 per capita as of 2020, significantly lower than many developed countries. Total greenhouse gas emissions by China are the world's largest. China has prioritized reducing pollution, announcing its aims to reach its peak emissions levels before 2030, and achieve carbon neutrality by 2060. Water quality in China has been impacted by rapid development and high levels of agricultural runoff and heavy metal pollution. China is the world's leading investor in renewable energy and its commercialization, investing CN¥3.6 trillion (US$546 billion) in 2022 alone. Traditionally reliant on non-renewable energy sources such as coal, China's adoption of renewable energy has increased significantly in the 2010s and 2020s. In 2025, 54.4% of China's electricity came from coal, while 41.6% came from clean energy, with the remainder from other fossil fuels.
title: China

text: Despite its emphasis on renewables, China remains dependent on global oil markets.
title: China

text: China is the second-largest country by land area after Russia, and the third or fourth largest by total area. Total area figures are generally around 9,596,961 km2 (3,705,407 sq mi). China borders 14 nations, with a combined land border length of 22,117 km (13,743 mi). Its coastline spans approximately 14,500 km (9,000 mi). The PRC has engaged in 23 border disputes since 1949, of which six remain unsettled. It actively disputes several portions of its Himalayan border with India, including Aksai Chin in Kashmir and the Indian state of Arunachal Pradesh, which led to military skirmishes in 2020. It maintains maritime disputes with Japan over the Senkaku/Diaoyu Islands and with various countries over a group of South China Sea Islands within the "Nine-dash line", including the Spratlys and Paracels. This has led to skirmishes with Vietnam and the Philippines. Both the PRC and the ROC on Taiwan claim legitimacy as the government of China, leading to cross-strait tensions.
title: China

text: Taiwan is a de jure province of the PRC, with the ROC-controlled islands of Kinmen and Matsu as a part of Fujian Province.
title: China

text: China is a unitary state under the absolute leadership of the Chinese Communist Party. Since the 1980s, the CCP has called its guiding theories and policies socialism with Chinese characteristics, which it considers an adapted form of Marxism–Leninism that emphasizes a market economy as the primary stage of socialism. China describes itself as a socialist state, and a people's democratic dictatorship. Many academic sources describe it as an authoritarian state, although others dispute this label as reductive, or as oversimplifying its methods of political control. The National People's Congress (NPC) holds the unified powers of the state and oversight over all state organs, with its Standing Committee elected to meet between the annual NPC meetings. NPC elections are indirect and the CCP controls nominations. The NPC elects the president, vice president, military chairman, and chief justice, and approves the president's nomination for premier (the head of government).
title: China

text: In practice, the CCP leadership chooses candidates for these posts. The premier heads the State Council, which includes 26 ministers, such as the heads of ministries and commissions. The Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference is an advisory body that formally leads the CCP's united front system, which aims to gain support from non-CCP intellectuals, eight minor parties, and people's organizations. China's current constitution dates to 1982, succeeding two earlier constitutions. Chinese governance is characterized by a high degree of political centralization but significant economic decentralization. Policy instruments and processes are often tested locally before being adopted more widely. Surveys have generally shown that the Chinese public has a high level of support for the government.
title: China

text: The CCP is the founding and sole ruling party of China, organized along Leninist principles as a vanguard party. With about 98 million members, it is among the world's largest political parties, as well as the longest continuously ruling. The party's highest body is its National Congress, which mainly consists of members elected by party membership and meets every five years. The National Congress elects the Central Committee, which convenes yearly as the highest party organ between congresses. The Central Committee ostensibly elects the party's top leadership, the Politburo, Politburo Standing Committee (PSC) and the general secretary, its top leader. In practice, the committee typically approves a slate of candidates created by existing party leadership. The Politburo usually gathers once a month, while the smaller PSC is thought to meet weekly. The current general secretary is Xi Jinping, who took office on 15 November 2012.
title: China

text: Xi concurrently serves as president and the chair of the Central Military Commission (CMC); as such, he is referred to informally as the paramount leader of China. The National Congress also elects the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection, the party's main disciplinary and anti-corruption organ. As the CCP is closely intertwined with the government, disputes within the party represent the main form of political contention in China. The CCP controls government appointments, with most senior officials being CCP members. The appointments of CCP cadres and the leadership of major state-owned enterprises and institutions are managed by the party's Organization Department. The Leninist principle of democratic centralism mandates that party decisions are binding on all members.
title: China

text: China is constitutionally a unitary state divided into 23 provinces, five autonomous regions (each with a designated minority group), four direct-administered municipalities, as well as the autonomous special administrative regions (SARs) of Hong Kong and Macau. Provinces and their equivalents are divided into prefectures and prefecture-level cities. These are divided into counties, county-level cities, and districts. Under these, townships are the basic form of local government. Direct elections occur only at the township and county levels and below.
title: China

text: China is one of five permanent members of the United Nations Security Council and the second largest contributor to the United Nations. China has the largest diplomatic network of any country: It has diplomatic relations with 179 United Nations member states and embassies in 174. China is a member of the G20, BRICS, East Asia Summit, APEC, and other intergovernmental organizations. China is widely described as a superpower due to its influence in geopolitics, technology, manufacturing, economics and culture. Although China moderated its relations with the West during the reform era, its rise in power has brought political tensions with many of its neighbors and with the United States, the current dominant superpower. Although China is among the United States' largest trade partners, their relationship is tempered by a trade war and disagreements over the political status of Taiwan.
title: China

text: China's foreign policy is based on the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence, which include a principle of non-intervention in other countries' domestic affairs. Per its policy of non-alignment, China has no defense pacts except for its 1961 treaty with North Korea, although it maintains close relationships with neighbors such as Pakistan and Russia. China has invested heavily in developing countries across Asia, Latin America, and Africa, creating a system of development banks and loans through the Belt and Road Initiative.
title: China

text: The People's Liberation Army (PLA) is the main armed forces of China, under the direct control of the CCP. It consists of four services: the Ground Force, the Navy, the Air Force, and the Rocket Force, and four arms: the Aerospace Force, the Cyberspace Force, the Information Support Force, and the Joint Logistics Support Force. It has around 2 million active soldiers, and the world's third largest stockpile of nuclear weapons, and the world's largest navy by ship count. The PLA is considered one of the world's most powerful militaries and has rapidly modernized in the 21st century. A 2026 study estimates that its 2025 expenditure was 2.27 trillion yuan (US$336 billion), 12% of global military spending and 1.7% of China's GDP. The PLA, the People's Armed Police and the Militia are commanded by the Central Military Commission. Due to the chairman responsibility system, the chairman of the CMC, currently Xi Jinping, is the commander-in-chief of the PLA.
title: China

text: The Chinese judicial system consists of people's courts at provincial, regional, and local levels, alongside circuit courts for regional matters and specialized courts to handle professional disputes. The highest legal authority is the Supreme People's Court. The courts are closely controlled by the CCP, supervised by corresponding people's congresses, and led by CCP appointees. PRC law derives from a combination of civil law, traditional Chinese law, and socialist law. China's law enforcement system is managed by the Ministry of Public Security, which oversees public security bureaus (PSBs) in each province, themselves divided into local levels. Local sub-bureaus and stations handle most routine policing. The People's Armed Police, a paramilitary force, is administered by the CMC and supports emergency response measures. The social credit system maintains a network of blacklists to record businesses and individuals who violate regulations, court orders, or financial agreements.
title: China

text: China has periodically mobilized anti-crime campaigns, using heavy penalties as a form of deterrence. Violent crimes are the highest priority for enforcement, although they occur at relatively low rates. Capital punishment has declined since the Mao era, but remains common; China has the most executions per year of any country.
title: China

text: Various human rights organizations, United Nations assessments, and foreign governments have accused China of severe human rights violations. It has been accused of political repression, torture, indefinite detention, restrictions on free speech and religious practice, excessive use of capital punishment, and the persecution of ethnic minorities.Although the Chinese constitution protects a wide variety of civil and political rights, these largely lack enforcement mechanisms. The petitioning system allows citizens to raise complaints of wrongdoing, although the concerns are often left unaddressed, and some petitioners have faced punitive arrest or incarceration. In the 21st century, China has participated extensively in the United Nations Human Rights Council, but remains strongly critical of international scrutiny of its human rights, seeing it as interference in its internal affairs.
title: China

text: In Xinjiang, China has restricted the civil rights of the Uyghurs, who face widespread discrimination, police crackdowns, and restrictions on Islamic religious practice and the use of the Uyghur language. China interred over a million Uyghurs in a network of internment camps in the late 2010s. These facilities have evolved into a system of prisons and forced labor. Several UN OHCHR experts have equated it to "enslavement as a crime against humanity". China has restricted the civil and political rights of Hong Kong residents. Since the 2019–2020 protests, China has cracked down on the pro-democracy movement in the SAR and removed much of its political autonomy. China has cracked down on political expression in Tibet and strengthened surveillance since the late 2000s, restricting residents from obtaining passports and most foreigners from entering the region. China does not recognize same-sex marriage or same-sex adoption, and regularly censors LGBTQ-related media.
title: China

text: Many Chinese hospitals provide sexual conversion therapy, viewing homosexuality as a mental disorder. LGBTQ rights advocates are surveilled and criminalized.
title: China

text: The modern PRC is often described by analysts as an example of state capitalism or party-state capitalism, with both market forces and the state playing a major role in the economy. Various state organs manage the economy according to the State Council's five-year plans. China describes its economic system as a socialist market economy, in which the market plays a decisive role in resource allocation under the control of a socialist state. The Chinese economy has expanded more than 20 times since 2000. It is now the second largest economy by GDP (135 trillion yuan) and the largest when adjusted for purchasing power parity. China has brought roughly 800 million people out of extreme poverty, more than any other country in history.
title: China

text: China is the world's leading manufacturing power, accounting for 28% of global manufacturing as of 2024; it is the largest producer of steel, rare earths, ships, and automobiles, as well as the largest exporter of electronics and textiles. The private sector constitutes the largest portion of the Chinese economy, with about 30–40% under state ownership. State-owned companies make less than 10% of exports, but are predominant in industries such as transportation, utilities, and financial services. Since the 1990s, China has decentralized its economic planning, with about 85% of government spending delegated to the provincial or local level, and local governments adapting national economic plans to suit local interests. China's main stock exchanges are Shanghai and Shenzhen. Its stock market is the second largest, behind the US. The Chinese banking system makes up a much larger share of the economy than most other countries.
title: China

text: Four state-owned banks hold about 40% of the sector's assets as of 2022. China has struggled to establish its currency, the renminbi (in units of yuan), as an international reserve currency; as of 2025, it is the seventh largest currency in foreign exchange reserves. About a third of China's workforce consists of domestic migrant workers, the floating population. The hukou system restricts citizens' access to services and utilities outside of their registered home, leading to pronounced inequalities between urban and rural workers. Especially in larger cities, only those with local hukou may be able to buy property, though hukou restrictions have loosened significantly in the 21st century. According to 2026 state data, China's urban unemployment rate was 5.0%. China has a high debt-to-GDP ratio (almost 300% in 2020), with household debt at about 65% of the GDP. China has faced a property sector crisis since 2020.
title: China

text: By the late 2010s, Chinese real estate assets far exceed the combined total of stocks, bonds, and deposits.
title: China

text: As the world's largest economy for much of its history, many inventions and scientific discoveries have been produced in China, including paper, printing, the compass, and gunpowder (referred to as the Four Great Inventions). China has pursued rapid technological development since the reform era. It has made great advances in the fields of artificial intelligence, robotics, and biotechnology, while the Xi administration has prioritized green technology and reducing Chinese dependence on foreign technology. It has emphasized technocratic leadership in the 2020s, promoting experts in scientific fields to national leadership positions, while bringing major private technology firms such as Tencent and Alibaba under state regulation. Geopolitical tensions have led Europe and the United States to restrict Chinese access to their technology, especially semiconductors, and launch sanctions targeting the telecommunications and electronics firm Huawei.
title: China

text: Since launching its first satellite in 1970, China has maintained an active space program. After the United States and the Soviet Union, China became the third to independently put astronauts into orbit, with a 2003 mission. The Chinese Lunar Exploration Program has sent multiple robotic landers to the Moon, the Planetary Exploration of China program has sent a lander and rover to Mars, and the Tiangong space station has hosted crewed operations in Low Earth orbit since 2021.
title: China

text: Since the 1990s, automobiles have become a common form of transport in China. According to state data, the Chinese highway network exceeded 6,000,000 km (3,700,000 mi) by the end of 2021, having grown 30% over the past decade. In addition to local and provincial routes, this network includes the national highways, which are divided between the ordinary highways (of various classes) and the national expressway system. China has the largest highway and rail systems in the world by capacity, along with the second longest rail network at roughly 165,000 km (102,526 mi). According to 2022 state data, over 95% of cities exceeding one million residents have access to high-speed rail. Out of the 50 busiest container ports, 18 are located in China, including the world's busiest, the Port of Shanghai. China has the largest domestic aviation market by passenger capacity, and maintains 262 airports as of 2025. Chinese cities are disparate in their level of infrastructure.
title: China

text: Tier-one cities such as Beijing and Shanghai have elaborate and advanced infrastructure networks, while smaller cities and rural areas often have outdated and underfunded transit and public utilities. Water resources in China are unevenly distributed. With industrialization and rapid development, the drier north has faced endemic water shortages. To combat this, the South–North Water Transfer Project pumps water from the Yangtze basin to supply northern cities.
title: China

text: The State Grid Corporation of China, the world's largest utility company, manages the electrical grid for most of the country, with the China Southern Power Grid as the electric utility in some southern provinces. Power generation is primarily managed by five state-owned corporations, alongside local and provincial utilities. Most of China's renewable energy comes from hydropower. The Three Gorges Dam is the world's largest power station by capacity. China has the largest number of internet users and websites of any country. According to state data, it has 1.125 billion internet users as of 2025, about 80% of its population. It has an extensive system of internet censorship. The Great Firewall, a system of internet controls and regulations, blocks access to many foreign websites. Users can circumvent it through virtual private networks, but these face occasional crackdowns. The Cyberspace Administration of China is the national internet regulator and censor.
title: China

text: Most telecommunications are operated by state-owned companies.
title: China

text: China has urbanized significantly since the 1980s. The percentage of the country's population living in urban areas increased from 20% in 1980 to over 68% in 2025, according to Chinese government figures, while the United Nations calculates the 2025 urbanization rate as 83.7%. Cities in China often include smaller towns and rural areas under their jurisdiction. Shanghai is its most populous city by urban area. Two urban agglomerations, the Pearl Delta and Yangtze Delta, contain many of the largest cities and tens of millions of people. The figures below are from the 2020 census and are only estimates of the urban populations within administrative city limits; a different ranking exists for total municipal populations. The large floating population of migrant workers make conducting censuses in urban areas difficult.
title: China

text: Following an optional two to three years of preschool, China has nine years of free compulsory education, generally with six years of elementary school and three years of junior high school. If they pass entrance examinations, students may then attend a senior high school, choosing between an academic or vocational track. The gaokao exams allow access to undergraduate higher education, with additional examinations required to attend postgraduate programs. As of 2022, 95% of junior high students continue to high school, while higher education has a 59.6% enrollment rate. As of 2022, China had 158 million students enrolled in compulsory school, and 46.5 million enrolled in higher education. There are over 200,000 elementary and junior high schools, over 22,000 secondary schools, and over 3,000 colleges and universities. Both private and public schools exist at all levels, with 10.6% of elementary and junior high students attending private schools.
title: China

text: China became the world's largest publisher of scientific papers in 2016. Foreign language programs are mandatory from 3rd grade. Generally focused on English, other languages are increasingly being taught, especially at the senior high level.
title: China

text: The vast majority of primary health care institutions in China offer both allopathic and traditional Chinese medicine (TCM). In 2017, there were approximately 9,000 community health centers in urban areas—which oversaw roughly 25,000 health stations—and 37,000 township health centers in rural areas. There were about 639,000 village clinics, which operate as independent, for-profit enterprises subsidized by the state. The National Health Commission, together with its local counterparts, oversees health policy. After the beginning of reform and opening-up in 1978, Chinese public health improved rapidly from better nutrition, although many free health services provided in the countryside disappeared. Healthcare in China became mostly privatized and experienced a significant quality increase. China is a major producer and exporter of active pharmaceutical ingredients. According to 2025 state data, the life expectancy at birth exceeds 79 years, and the infant mortality rate is 4 per 1,000.
title: China

text: Rates of stunted growth declined from 33.1% in 1990 to 4.5% in 2024. Mental health services are underfunded and unevenly distributed. The COVID-19 pandemic was first identified in Wuhan. China maintained a zero-COVID policy, using lockdowns, quarantines, and contact tracing to curb its transmission, until protests in November–December 2022.
title: China

text: Beginning in the Qin and Han dynasties and continuing over the following millennia, an area of Chinese cultural influence grew to encompass much of East Asia. Japan, Korea, and Vietnam adopted various political, philosophical, religious, and aesthetic concepts from China, facilitated by their adoption of Chinese characters and participation in the tributary system. China has 60 World Heritage Sites, including the Great Wall and Grand Canal, the second most of any country (behind Italy). Chinese culture has historically emphasized family connections, with filial piety and the veneration of ancestors seen as vital duties under Confucian ethics. Prior to the 20th century, family relations were highly patriarchal, and arranged marriages were commonplace. The CCP pushed for gender equality after coming to power, establishing the All-China Women's Federation to manage women's issues.
title: China

text: However, many patriarchal gender norms remain prevalent, and women face lower employment rates and occupational gender segregation. Prior to the adoption of the Gregorian calendar in 1912, China traditionally used a 12-month lunisolar calendar. The 60-part sexagenary cycle was often used to enumerate days as well as years, alongside the twelve-year Chinese zodiac. Major holidays and festivals in China include the Chinese New Year (or Spring Festival), the Qingming Festival, the Mid-Autumn Festival, and National Day.
title: China

text: Traditional Chinese art makes use of a wide array of common motifs, metaphors, and symbols, often using nature as allegory. During the imperial era, skill in art was a marker of refinement and high social status. By the Song period, landscape paintings became among the most prestigious genres. Renowned art pieces often bear inscriptions and seals from their previous owners, allowing for the tracing of provenance over long periods of time. Chinese paintings are traditionally made with ink brushes on paper or silk. Horizontal handscrolls and vertical hanging scrolls are common formats, alongside wall paintings, folding screens and hand fans. Calligraphy, emerging during the 3rd and 4th centuries CE, was traditionally regarded in China as the most prestigious form of art, and remains among the most widely practiced. Western painting styles gained popularity during the early 20th century, while the Mao government promoted art as a means to embody socialist ideals.
title: China

text: The 21st century has seen a boom in the international influence of Chinese contemporary art. Pottery and metal crafts in China date to ancient times. Porcelain, also known as china, became a common form of ceramic during the 7th century. By the 14th century, it became popular to decorate porcelain vessels with elaborate blue and white patterns, which became the most popular form of Chinese ceramics. Jade crafts and lacquerware have been common decorative mediums since antiquity.
title: China

text: Wood is the most commonly used material in traditional Chinese architecture. Roofs of important buildings, generally ceramic tile, are often ornate and hipped. Traditional buildings are often arranged around cardinal directions, with grandeur expressed through large complexes, often featuring courtyards and large gates. The spiritual concept of feng shui influences the layout of houses and settlements, oriented around the flow of qi, vital energy. Pagodas, multi-story religious towers far taller than other forms of traditional architecture, were introduced to China alongside Buddhism, and comprise many of China's oldest buildings. Western-style architecture was introduced during the 1800s, while domestic architects began to implement Western design principles in the 1900s. The reform era has seen a boom in contemporary skyscrapers and offices, which have largely supplanted traditional architecture.
title: China

text: The music of China is highly diverse and regional. Traditional Chinese music uses a wide variety of instruments, including the dizi (a flute), erhu (a bowed string instrument), guqin (a plucked string instrument), guzheng (a plucked zither), pipa (a lute), sheng (a mouth organ), suona (a wind instrument), and various types of bells and drums. Western-style music spread during the early 20th century, leading the Chinese orchestra to develop as a fusion of Western orchestral music with Chinese instruments. Western classical music remains highly prestigious. Inspired by Western jazz and boosted by the introduction of recording studios, Mandarin pop music emerged in Shanghai in the 1920s, while the folk rock-inspired Cantopop became popular around Hong Kong during the 1970s. After reform and opening-up, various forms of pop and rock music reached widespread popularity. Chinese opera emerged from shuochang, folk narrative singing traditions.
title: China

text: Influenced by various regional traditions and kunqu, a genre popular during the Ming dynasty, Peking opera reached national popularity during the Qing dynasty, while various local and regional forms of opera emerged across the country. Maoist China promoted revolutionary opera and communist-oriented folk music. By the Han period, Chinese dance was a frequent subject of art and poetry, as well as an element of religious rites. Dancers often performed for the imperial courts, while Chinese opera dances led to increasing numbers of dance troupes across all levels of society during the Qing. Western dances gained popularity in the early 20th century, while the CCP promoted folk dances such as yangge.
title: China

text: Chinese meals generally incorporate a grain (fan) alongside meat or vegetable-based dishes (cai). Flour—as steamed buns, dumplings, pancakes, or noodles—is the primary grain in the north, alongside maize, millet, rice, and in some regions, sorghum. Rice—steamed or in the form of congee, rice noodles or rice cakes—dominates in the south. Although Chinese cuisine is highly diverse and regional, pork, chicken, fish, and duck are the most common meats. Soybeans are a common staple nationally made into products such as tofu and soy sauce. Stir frying in woks is the most common cooking method, alongside deep-frying, steaming, and hot pot, where dishes are cooked in simmering broth at the table. People in China generally eat three meals a day, often with a simple breakfast and a more elaborate dinner. Chopsticks are the main eating utensil. Dishes are usually served to be shared among multiple people, rather than served in individual portions.
title: China

text: Hot tea almost always accompanies meals across the country, in lieu of water. Alcohol such as rice wines and the distilled liquor baijiu are commonly served with meals. Chinese cuisine was traditionally divided into four great traditions: Lu (Shandong), Yang (Jiangsu), Chuan (Sichuan), and Yue (Guangdong). Chinese Buddhists have developed a unique cuisine that avoids meat, while Chinese Islamic cuisine excludes pork and alcohol.
title: China

text: Various forms of robe served as the main form of clothing for men and women throughout Chinese history, adapting over the centuries. Silk, hemp, and later cotton were the main textiles. Both men and women generally bound their hair with caps or pins, except during periods where foreign hairstyles were enforced by the elite. Chinese fashions changed greatly during the 20th century, as traditional designs largely gave way to Western clothing. The qipao became a popular form of women's dress during the early 20th century, but are today rare outside of formal occasions. After a focus on simple, practical clothing during the Mao era, the reform era saw the emergence of a Western-style fashion industry. In the 21st century, the Hanfu movement has sought to promote a reconstructed form of traditional Chinese clothing.
title: China

text: China has among the longest continuous literary traditions in the world. Late Shang-era oracle bone inscriptions are the oldest known form of Chinese writing, while the oldest surviving literary works—such as the Book of Documents—date to the early Zhou. The Chinese literary canon was historically centered on the Five Classics (ancient transmitted texts) and the Four Books (central Confucian texts). Writings on history were ubiquitous and closely connected to literature since ancient times, seen as a way to guide later generations. The literati regarded literature as primarily didactic, with fiction seen as useless and potentially corruptive. However, poetry was viewed highly for its ability to convey the nature of reality. The poetry of the Tang era was particularly prized in later dynasties. Before the early 20th century, fiction was generally written in vernacular Chinese, with formal works generally in Classical Chinese.
title: China

text: Popular vernacular literature spread with the introduction of printing, resulting in works such as the Four Classic Novels of the Ming and Qing periods. Modern Chinese literature has been heavily influenced by the political upheavals of the 19th and 20th centuries, seeking to explain the political climate or imagine its future. New Culture writers such as Lu Xun promoted the importance of fiction and vernacular Chinese, experimenting with new modernist forms, while writers of the Reform era sought to explain the trauma of the Mao era. Chinese online literature has become popular alongside the growth of the internet, with about half of Chinese internet users regularly consuming it.
title: China

text: Traditional sports such as martial arts and dragon boat racing have been practiced in China for over a millennium. The ball game cuju predates the Qin dynasty and remained popular for millennia, declining during the late Qing dynasty. Chuiwan (similar to modern golf) and polo were popular sports among elites throughout portions of the imperial period, while commoners played regional ball games. Evolving out of Chinese martial arts in the Qing period, tai chi incorporates Taoist practices into a form of gymnastics. Modern sporting was introduced to China from the West during the late 19th and early 20th centuries. China first participated in the Olympic Games in 1932. Although association football draws large audiences, the men's national team has only qualified once for the FIFA World Cup; the country hosted the FIFA Women's World Cup twice and the women's team finished as runners-up once.
title: China

text: China began to invest heavily in elite sports during the 1990s, and in 2008 Beijing hosted the Summer Olympics. Elite sports in China are managed by the General Administration of Sport, which oversees management centers for various sports, as well as provincial sports committees and teams. The vast majority of sports funding, especially for elite sports, comes from the government. China hosted the Winter Olympics in 2022, and the Asian Games in 1990, 2010, and 2022. China is dominant among international competition in table tennis (often dubbed China's national sport), badminton, diving, and weightlifting, and is among the top global competitors in snooker. Various card, dice, and board games gained popularity in imperial China, most notably weiqi (also known as Go) and xiangqi (a relative of chess). Mahjong emerged during the 1800s, initially one of many popular gambling games. China is the world's largest video game market.
title: China

text: Video games were introduced from Japan in the 1980s, and online video games grew to immense popularity alongside the spread of the internet.

text: चीन (चीनी: 中国),आधिकारिक रूप से चीन जनवादी गणराज्य (चीनी: 中华人民共和国), पूर्वी एशिया का एक देश है। यह विश्व का दूसरा सर्वाधिक जनसंख्या वाला देश है, जिसकी जनसंख्या 1.4 अरब से अधिक है। चीन पाँच समय क्षेत्रों के बराबर फैला हुआ है और 14 देशों की भूमि से सीमाएँ हैं, विश्व के किसी भी देश से सर्वाधिक, रूस के साथ बन्धा हुआ है। लगभग 96 लाख वर्ग किमी के क्षेत्रफल के साथ, यह कुल भूमि क्षेत्र के हिसाब से विश्व का तृतीय सबसे बड़ा देश है। देश में 22 प्रान्त, पाँच स्वायत्त क्षेत्र, चार नगर पालिकाएँ और दो विशेष प्रशासनिक क्षेत्र (हॉङ्कॉङ और मकाउ) अन्तर्गत हैं। राष्ट्रीय राजधानी बीजिंग है, और सर्वाधिक जनसंख्या वाला नगर और वित्तीय केन्द्र शंघाई है। चीन विश्व की प्राचीन सभ्यताओं। इसकी सभ्यता एवं संस्कृति छठी शताब्दी से भी पुरानी है। चीन की लिखित भाषा प्रणाली विश्व की सबसे पुरानी है जो आज तक उपयोग में लायी जा रही है और जो कई आविष्कारों का स्रोत भी है। ब्रिटिश विद्वान और जीव-रसायन शास्त्री जोसफ नीधम ने प्राचीन चीन के चार महान अविष्कार बताये जो हैं :- कागज़, कम्पास, बारूद और मुद्रण।
title: China

text: ऐतिहासिक रूप से चीनी संस्कृति का प्रभाव पूर्वी और दक्षिण पूर्वी एशियाई देशों पर रहा है और चीनी धर्म, रिवाज़ और लेखन प्रणाली को इन देशों में अलग-अलग स्तर तक अपनाया गया है। चीन में प्रथम मानवीय उपस्थिति के प्रमाण झोऊ कोऊ दियन गुफा के समीप मिलते हैं और जो होमो इरेक्टस के प्रथम नमूने भी है जिसे हम 'पेकिंग मानव' के नाम से जानते हैं। अनुमान है कि ये इस क्षेत्र में ३,००,००० से ५,००,००० वर्ष पूर्व यहाँ रहते थे और कुछ शोधों से ये महत्वपूर्ण जानकारी भी मिली है कि पेकिंग मानव आग जलाने की और उसे नियंत्रित करने की कला जानते थे। आधुनिक चीनी अपनी उत्पत्ति उत्तरी चीन के मैदान में पीली नदी के उपजाऊ बेसिन में सभ्यता के उद्गम स्थल में खोजते हैं 21वीं शताब्दी ईसा पूर्व में अर्ध-पौराणिक शिया राजवंश और अच्छी तरह से प्रमाणित षाङ और झोउ राजवंशों ने वंशानुगत राजशाही, या राजवंशों की सेवा के लिए एक नौकरशाही राजनीतिक प्रणाली विकसित की। इस अवधि के दौरान चीनी लिपि, चीनी उत्कृष्ट साहित्य और सौ विचारधाराएँ उभरे और आने वाली शताब्दियों तक चीन और उसके पड़ोसियों को प्रभावित किया।
title: China

text: तीसरी शताब्दी ईसा पूर्व में, छिन के एकीकरण के युद्धों ने प्रथम चीनी साम्राज्य, अल्पकालिक छिन राजवंश का निर्माण किया। छिन के बाद अधिक स्थिर हान राजवंश (206 ईसा पूर्व-220 सीई) आया, जिसने लगभग दो सहस्राब्दी के लिए एक मॉडल स्थापित किया जिसमें चीनी साम्राज्य विश्व की अग्रणी आर्थिक शक्तियों में से एक था। साम्राज्य का विस्तार हुआ, खण्डित हुआ, और पुन: एकीकृत हुआ; जीत लिया गया और पुनः स्थापित किया गया; विदेशी धर्मों और विचारों को अवशोषित किया; और विश्व-अग्रणी वैज्ञानिक प्रगति की, जैसे चार महान आविष्कार: बारूद, काग़ज़, दिक्सूचक, और मुद्रण। हान के पतन के बाद शताब्दियों की एकता के बाद, सुई (581–618) और थाङ (618–907) राजवंशों ने साम्राज्य को फिर से एकीकृत किया। बहु-जातीय थाङ ने विदेशी व्यापार और संस्कृति का स्वागत किया जो कौशेय मार्ग पर आया और बौद्ध धर्म को चीनी आवश्यकताओं के अनुकूल बनाया। प्रारम्भिक आधुनिक सुङ राजवंश (960-1279) वृद्धि से नगरी और वाणिज्यिक बन गया।
title: China

text: नागरिक विद्वानधिकारियों या साहित्यकारों ने पहले के राजवंशों के सैन्य अभिजात वर्ग को बदलने के लिए परीक्षा प्रणाली और नव-कन्फ़्यूशीवाद के सिद्धान्तों का उपयोग किया। मंगोल आक्रमण ने 1279 में युऐन राजवंश की स्थापना की, लेकिन मिङ राजवंश (1368-1644) ने हान चीनी नियंत्रण को फिर से स्थापित किया। मांछु के नेतृत्व वाले छिङ राजवंश ने साम्राज्य के क्षेत्र को लगभग दोगुना कर दिया और एक बहु-जातीय राज्य की स्थापना की जो आधुनिक चीनी राष्ट्र का आधार था, लेकिन 19वीं शताब्दी में विदेशी साम्राज्यवाद को भारी क्षति उठाना पड़ा। चीन वर्तमान में चीनी साम्यवादी दल द्वारा एकात्मक मार्क्सवादी-लेनिनवादी एक-दलीय समाजवादी गणराज्य के रूप में शासित है। चीन संयुक्त राष्ट्र सुरक्षा परिषद का स्थायी सदस्य है और एशियाई आधारभूत संरचना निवेश बैंक, कौशेय मार्ग कोष, नूतन विकास बैंक, षंख़ाई सहयोग संगठन और क्षेत्रीय व्यापक आर्थिक भागीदारी जैसे कई बहुपक्षीय और क्षेत्रीय सहयोग संगठनों का संस्थापक सदस्य है। यह ब्रिक्स, जी8+5, जी-20, एशिया - प्रशांत महासागरीय आर्थिक सहयोग और पूर्वी एशिया शिखर सम्मेलन का भी सदस्य है।
title: China

text: यह लोकतंत्र, नागरिक स्वातंत्र्य, सरकार की पारदर्शिता, प्रेस की स्वतंत्रता, धर्म स्वातंत्र्य और जातीय अल्पसंख्यकों के मानवाधिकारों के माप में सबसे नीचे है। मानवाधिकार कार्यकर्ताओं और गैर-सरकारी संगठनों द्वारा राजनीतिक दमन, व्यापक अभिवेचन, अपने नागरिकों की व्यापक निगरानी, ​​और विरोध और असन्तोष के हिंसक दमन सहित मानवाधिकारों के हनन के लिए चीनी अधिकारियों की आलोचना की गई है। विश्व अर्थव्यवस्था का लगभग पंचम भाग बनाते हुए, चीन क्रय-शक्ति समता पर जीडीपी के हिसाब से विश्व की सबसे बड़ी अर्थव्यवस्था है, सकल घरेलू उत्पाद के हिसाब से दूसरी सबसे बड़ी अर्थव्यवस्था है, और दूसरा सबसे धनी देश है। देश सबसे वृद्धि से बढ़ती प्रमुख अर्थव्यवस्थाओं में से एक है और विश्व का सबसे बड़ा निर्माता और निर्यातक है, साथ ही दूसरा सबसे बड़ा आयातक भी है। सैन्य कर्मियों द्वारा विश्व की सबसे बड़ी स्थायी सेना और दूसरा सबसे बड़ा रक्षा बजट वाला चीन एक मान्यता प्राप्त परमाण्वस्त्र वाला देश है।
title: China

text: चीन को अपने उच्च स्तर के नवाचार, आर्थिक क्षमता, बढ़ती सैन्य ताकत और अंतर्राष्ट्रीय मामलों में प्रभाव के कारण संभावित महाशक्ति माना जाता है।
title: China

text: चीन में सामान्य रूप से प्रयुक्त होने वाले नाम हैं "झोङ्ह्वा" (中华/中華) और "झोंग्वौ" (中国/中國), जबकि चीनी मूल के लोगों को आमतौर पर "हान" (汉/漢) और "थाङ्" (唐) नाम दिया जाता है। अन्य प्रयुक्त होने वाले नाम हैं हुआश़िया, शेन्झोउ और जिझोउ। चीनी जनवादी गणराज्य (中华人民共和国) और चीनी गणराज्य (中国共和国) उन दो सम्प्रभू देशों के आधिकारिक नाम है जो पारम्परिक रूप से चीन नाम से जाने जाने वाले क्षेत्र पर अपनी दावेदारी करते हैं। "मुख्यभूमि चीन" उन क्षेत्रों के सन्दर्भ में प्रयुक्त किया जाता है जो क्षेत्र चीनी जनवादी गणराज्य के अधीन हैं और इसमें हांग कांग और मकाउ सम्मिलित नहीं हैं। "चीन" शब्द का प्रथम दर्ज उपयोग १५५५ में किया गया था। ये शब्द चिन से निकला था जो मार्को पोलो द्वारा पश्चिम में प्रचारित किया गया। यह किन साम्राज्य से निकला (秦) (७७८ ईसा पूर्व -२०७ ईसा पूर्व), जो झोऊ वंशावली के समय चीन का सबसे पश्चिमी साम्राज्य था। ऐतिहासिक रूप से चीन को सिना या सिनो, सिने, कैथे, या पश्चिमी देशों द्वारा सेरेस के नाम से भी जाना जाता है।
title: China

text: चीन का आधिकारिक नाम प्रत्येक वंश के साथ बदलता रहा है और सबसे प्रचलित और आम नाम है झोंग्गुओ (中國), जिसका अर्थ है "केंद्रीय राष्ट्र", या "मध्य साम्राज्य"। विश्व के अन्य भागों में, चीन के लिए बहुत से नाम उपयोग में हैं, जिनमें से अधिकतर "किन" या "जिन" और हान या तान के लिप्यन्तरण हैं। हिन्दी में प्रयुक्त नाम भी इसी लिप्यन्तरण से लिया गया है।
title: China

text: चीन में सबसे अधिक बौद्ध धर्म मानने वाले लोग हैं । मूल चीनी धर्म जैसे ताओ धर्म, कुन्फ़्यूशियसी धर्म के अधिकांश अनुयायी भी बौद्ध धर्म का पालन करते है।
title: China

text: चीन में धर्म जीवन पद्धति है चीन में धर्म की स्थिति अन्य देशों जैसी नहीं है। भारत में या अन्यत्र किसी को हिन्दू, मुस्लिम, ईसाई, बौद्ध, यहुदी आदि धर्मों का अनुयायी बताया जाता है पर चीन में एेसा नहीं है। चीन में कोई व्यक्ति अपनी पारिवारिक और नैतिक समस्याओं के निराकरण के लिये कन्फ्यूशियानिज्म की शरण में चला जाता है, वही व्यक्ति स्वास्थ्य तथा मनोवैज्ञानिक चिन्ताओं के लिये ताओवाद अपना लेता है, अपने स्वजनों के अन्तिम संस्कार के लिये बौद्ध धर्म की परम्पराएं स्वीकार करता है और अन्य बातों के लिये वह स्थानीय देवी देवताओं की आराधना करता है।
title: China

text: वर्तमान में चीन में सभी धर्मों का अनुसरण किया जाता है। यहां के मुख्य धर्म हैं- बौद्ध, ताओ और अल्पसंख्यक धर्म हैं- इस्लाम व ईसाई। इनके अलावा अति अल्प संख्या में हिन्दू तथा यहुदी धर्मों के अनुयायी भी यहां हैं। आज से 4000 वर्ष पूर्व चीन में लोग भिन्न भिन्न देवताओं की पूजा करते थे जैसे मौसम के देवता या आकाश के देवता और इनसे ऊपर एक अन्य देवता शांग ली। इस जमाने में लोग विश्वास करते थे कि उनके पूर्वज मरने के बाद देवता बन गये इसलिये हर परिवार अपने पूर्वजों को पूजता था। बाद में जाकर लोगों को यह विश्वास होने लगा कि सबसे बड़ा देवता वह है जो तमाम अन्य देवताओं पर शासन करता है। स्वर्ग देवता अर्थात् तीयन ही चीन के सम्राट और साम्राज्ञी तय करता था। 2500 साल पहले चीनी धर्म में नये विचारों का आगमन हुआ। लाओ जू नामक दार्शनिक ने ताओवाद की स्थापना की जो बहुत लोकप्रिय हुआ। इस धर्म का मुख्य आधार यह था कि लोगों को जबर्दस्ती अपनी इच्छाएं नहीं पूरी करनी चाहिये वरन् समझ और सहकार से जीना चाहिये। यह एक दर्शन भी था और धर्म भी। इसी काल में एक अन्य दार्शनिक कन्फ्यूशियस का उदय हुआ जिनका दर्शन ताओवाद से भिन्न था।
title: China

text: इस वाद के अनुसार लोगों को अपने कर्तव्य पूरे करने चाहिये, अपने नेताओं का अनुसरण करना चाहिये तथा अपने देवताओं पर श्रद्धा रखनी चाहिये। इस वाद का मूल मंत्र व्यवस्था थी। इन नये धर्मों के बावजूद लोग अपने प्राचीन धर्मों पर चलते रहे और पूर्वजों को पूजते रहे।
title: China

text: 2000 वर्ष पूर्व बौद्ध धर्म का चीन में आगमन हुआ और चीनी जनजीवन में अत्यन्त लोकप्रिय हो गया। बौद्ध धर्म चीन का सर्वाधिक संगठित धर्म है तथा आज समूचे विश्व में सबसे अधिक बौद्ध अनुयायी चीन में ही है। कई चीनी ताओ तथा बौद्ध धर्म दोनों को एक साथ मानते हैं। ईसाई धर्म का आगमन 1860 में पहले अफीम युद्ध के दौरान हुआ। इस्लाम का पदार्पण सन् 651 में यहां हुआ।
title: China

text: चीन में धर्म जीवन पद्धति है, यह दर्शन है और आध्यात्म है। चीन की जनवादी सरकार आधिकारिक रूप से नास्तिक है मगर यह अपने नागरिकों को धर्म और उपासना की स्वतंत्रता देती है। लेनिन व माओ के काल में धार्मिक विश्वासों और उनके अनुपालन पर प्रतिबन्ध लगा दिया गया था। तमाम विहारों, पेगोडा, मस्जिदों और चर्चों को अधार्मिक भवनों में बदल दिया गया था। 1970 के अन्त में जाकर इस नीति को शिथिल किया गया और लोगों को धार्मिक अनुसरण की इजाजत दी जाने लगी। 1990 के बाद से पूरे चीन में बौद्ध तथा ताओ विहारों या मन्दिरों के पुनर्निर्माण का विशाल कार्यक्रम शुरू हुआ। 2007 में चीनी संविधान में एक नई धारा जोड़कर धर्म को नागरिकों के जीवन का महत्वपूर्ण तत्व स्वीकार किया गया।
title: China

text: एक सर्वेक्षण के अनुसार चीन की 50 से 80 प्रतिशत जनसंख्या 66 कराेड़ से 1 अरब तक लोग बौद्ध हैं जबकि ताओ सिर्फ 30 प्रतिशत या 40 करोड़ ही हैं। चूँकि अधिकांश चीनी दोनों धर्मों को मानते हैं इसलिये इन आँकड़ों में दोनों का समावेश हो सकता है। एक अन्य सर्वेक्षण के अनुसार चीन की 91 प्रतिशत जनसंख्या या 1 अरब 25 करोड़ लोग बौद्ध धर्म के अनुयायी है। ईसाई 4 से 5 करोड़ और इस्लाम को मानने वाले 2 करोड़ के लगभग हैं अर्थात् डेढ़ प्रतिशत।
title: China

text: बौद्ध धर्म को सरकार का मौन समर्थन प्राप्त है। दो वर्ष पूर्व सरकार ने ही यहां विश्व बौद्ध सम्मेलन का आयोजन किया था। विश्व की सबसे बड़ी बौद्ध प्रतिमा हेनान में सन् 2002 में स्थापित की गई थी। हेनान की प्रतिमा स्प्रिंग टैम्पल बुद्ध 502 फीट ऊँची है। दूसरे नम्बर पर म्यानमार की 360 फीट ऊँची बुद्ध प्रतिमा है जो कुछ वर्ष ही स्थापित की गई थी। जापान की 328 फीट ऊँची बौद्ध प्रतिमा 1995 में स्थापित हुई थी।
title: China

text: चीन की सभ्यता विश्व की प्राचीनतम सभ्यताओं में से एक है। इसका चार हज़ार वर्ष पुराना लिखित इतिहास है। यहां विभिन्न प्रकार के ऐतिहासिक व सांस्कृतिक ग्रन्थ और पुरातन संस्कृति के अवशेष पाए गए हैं। दुनिया के अन्य राष्ट्रों के समान चीनी राष्ट्र भी अपने विकास के दौरान आदिम समाज, दास समाज और सामन्ती समाज के कालों से गुजरा था। ऐतिहासिक विकास के इस लम्बे दौर में, चीनी राष्ट्र की विभिन्न जातियों की परिश्रमी, साहसी और बुद्धिमान जनता ने अपने संयुक्त प्रयासों से एक शानदार और ज्योतिर्मय संस्कृति का सृजन किया, तथा समूची मानवजाति के लिये भारी योगदान भी किया। यह उन गिनी-चुनी सभ्यताओं में से एक है जिन्होंने प्राचीन काल में अपनी स्वतन्त्र लेखन पद्धति का विकास किया। अन्य सभ्यताओं के नाम हैं - प्राचीन भारत की सिन्धु घाटी सभ्यता, मेसोपोटामिया की सभ्यता, मिस्र और दक्षिण अमेरिका की माया सभ्यता। चीनी लिपि अब भी चीन, जापान के साथ-साथ आंशिक रूप से कोरिया तथा वियतनाम में प्रयुक्त होती है। कदाचित् इसीलिये भारत तथा फारस के प्राचीन निवासियों ने इस देश का नाम अपने यहाँ 'चीन' रख लिया था।
title: China

text: यहाँ के रेशमी कपड़े भारत में 'चीनांशुक' नाम से इतने प्रसिद्ध थे कि रेशमी कपड़े का नाम ही 'चीनांशुक' पड़ गया है। चीन में बहुत प्राचीन काल का क्रमबद्ध इतिहास सुरक्षित है। ईसा से २९५० वर्ष पूर्व तक के राजवंश का पता चलता है। चीन की सभ्यता बहुत प्राचीन है, यहाँ तक कि यूरोप की सभ्यता का बहुत कुछ अंश— जैसे, पहनावा, बैठने और खाने पीने आदि का ढंग, पुस्तक छापने की कला आदि — चीन से लिया गया है। यहाँ ईसा के २२१७ वर्ष पूर्व से बौद्ध धर्म का संचार हो गया था पर ईसवीं सन् ६१ में मिंगती राजा के शासनकाल में जब भारतवर्ष से ग्रंथ और मूर्तियाँ गई, लोग बौद्ध धम्म की ओर आकर्षित होने लगे। सन् ६७ में कश्यप मतंग नामक एक बौद्ध भिक्खू चीन में गए और उन्होंने 'द्वाचत्वारिंशत् सूत्र' का चीनी भाषा में अनुवाद किया। तबसे बराबर चीन में बौद्ध धम्म का प्रचार बढ़ता गया। चीन से झुंड के झुंड यात्री विद्याध्ययन के लिये भारतवर्ष में आते थे। चीन में अब तक ऐसे कई स्तूप पाये जाते हैं जिनके विषय में चीनियों का कथन है कि वे सम्राट अशोक के बनवाये हुए हैं। चीन नें भारत समेत दुनिया के १५ देशों पर ६०० वर्ष शासन किया।
title: China

text: पुरातात्विक साक्ष्यों के आधार पर चीन में मानव बसावट लगभग साढ़े बाईस लाख वर्ष पुराना है।

text: १९४९ में अपनी स्थापना से १९७८ के उत्तरकाल तक, चीनी जनवादी गणराज्य एक सोवियत-शैली के समान एक केन्द्रीय नियोजित अर्थव्यस्था थी। निजी व्यापार और पूंजीवाद अनुपस्थित थे। देश के एक आधुनिक, औद्योगिक साम्यवादी समाज बनाने के लिए माओत्से तुंग ने प्रगल्भ दीर्घ छलांग की स्थापना की थी। माओ की मृत्यु और सांस्कृतिक क्रान्ति के अन्त के बाद, देंग जियाओपिंग और नए चीनी नेतृत्व में अर्थव्यवस्था में सुधार और एक दलीय शासन के अधीन एक बाज़ार-उन्मुख मिश्रित अर्थव्यवस्था बनाने के लिए सुधार आरम्भ किए। १९७८ से, चीन और जापान के राजनयिक सम्बन्ध सामान्य रहे हैं और चीन ने जापान से सुलभ ऋण लेने का निर्णय लिया। १९७८ से जापान, चीन में प्रथम विदेशी ऋणदाता रहा है। चीन की अर्थव्यवस्था मुख्य रूप से निजी सम्पत्ति के स्वामित्व पर आधारित एक बाज़ार अर्थव्यवस्था के रूप में चित्रित है। कृषि का सामूहीकरण हटा दिया गया और कृषिभूमि का उत्पादकता बढ़ाने के लिए निजीकरण किया गया। विस्तृत विविधता वाले लघु उद्यमों को प्रोत्साहित किया गया, जबकि सरकार ने मूल्य नियन्त्रण और विदेशी निवेश को बढ़ावा दिया।
title: China

text: विदेश व्यापार पर विकास के एक प्रमुख वाहन के समान ध्यान दिया गया, जो विशेष आर्थिक क्षेत्रों (विआक्षे) के निर्माण की ओर उन्मुख हुआ और शेन्ज़ेन (हांगकांग के निकट) में प्रथम और बाद में अन्य चीनी नगरों शहरों में विआक्षे का निर्माण हुआ। राज्य के स्वामित्व वाले अक्षम उद्यमों (रास्वाउ) का पश्चिमी शैली की प्रबन्धन प्रणाली के आधार पर पुनर्गठन किया गया और लाभहीन वाले बन्द कर दिए गए, जिसके कारण बेरोज़गारी में भी वृद्धि हुई। १९७८ में आर्थिक उदारीकरण प्रारम्भ होने से लेकर अब तक, चीजग की निवेश-और-निर्यात-आधारित अर्थव्यवस्था आकार में ९० गुणा बढ़ गई है और विश्व की प्रमुख अर्थव्यवस्थाओं में सबसे तेज़ी से बढ़ती अर्थव्यवस्था है। संज्ञात्मक सकल घरेलू उत्पाद के आधार पर यह अब दुनिया की दूसरी सबसे बड़ी अर्थव्यवस्था है जिसकी संज्ञात्मक जीडीपी ३४.०६ खरब यूआन (४.९९ खरब अमेरिकी $) है, यद्यपि इसकी प्रति व्यक्ति आय अभी भी ३,७०० अमेरिकी $ ही है जो चीजग को कम से कम सौ देशों से पीछे रखता है। प्राथमिक, गौण और तृतीयक उद्योगों का २००९ में अर्थव्यवस्था में क्रमशः १०.६%, ४६.८% और ४२.६% योगदान था।
title: China

text: क्रय शक्ति के आधार पर भी चीजग ९.०५ खरब $ के साथ विश्व की दूसरी सबसे बड़ी अर्थव्यवस्था है जो प्रति व्यक्ति ६,८०० बैठता है। चीजग ने पिछले एक दशक में औसतन १०.३% की दर से उन्नति की है जबकि अमेरिका के लिए यह आँकड़ा १.८% है। स्टैण्डर्ड चार्टेड का अनुमान है कि वृद्धि दर अगले दशक के मध्य तक ८% रह जाएगी और २०२७ से २०३० के मध्य ५% तक रहेगी। नवम्बर २०१० में जापान की सरकार ने कहा कि चीन, जो विश्व का सबसे बड़ा मोबाइल फ़ोन, कम्प्यूटर और वाहन निर्माता है, में उत्पादन में सितम्बर २०१० से आरम्भ तिमाही में जापान को पछाड़ चुका है। चीन की अर्थव्यवस्था ने २००५ में ब्रिटेन और २००७ में जर्मनी की अर्थव्यवस्थाओं को पछाड़ दिया था। चीजन विश्व का सर्वाधिक पधारा जाने वाला देश है जहाँ २००९ में ५ करोड़ ९ लाख अन्तर्राष्ट्रीय पर्यटक पधारे थे। यह विश्व व्यापार संगठन (विव्यास) का सदस्य है और विश्व की दूसरी सबसे बड़ी व्यापारिक शक्ति है जिसका कुल अन्तर्राष्ट्रीय व्यापार २.२१ खरब अमेरिकी $ (१.२० खरब निर्यात (#१) और १.०१ खरब आयात (#२)) था। इसका विदेशी मुद्रा भण्डार २.४ खरब $ है जो विश्व में बड़े अन्तर से सर्वाधिक है।

text: चीजग एक अनुमान के अनुसार १.६ खरब $ की अमेरिकी प्रतिभूतियों का स्वामी है। चीजग, ८०१.५ अरब $ के राजकोषीय (ट्रेज़री) बॉण्ड के साथ, संराअमेरिका के सार्वजनिक ऋण का सबसे बड़ा विदेशी धारक है। २००८ में चीजग ने ९२.४ अरब $ का प्रत्यक्ष विदेशी निवेश (प्रविनि) आकर्षित किया जो विश्व में तीसरा सर्वाधिक था यह और स्वयं चीजग ने भी विदेशो में ५२.२ अरब $ निवेश किए जो विश्व में छठा सर्वाधिक था।

text: चीनी भाषा विश्व की सर्वाधिक बोली जाने वाली भाषा है। दरसल चीन के विभिन्न लोगों द्वारा जो भाषाएँ बोली जाती हैं उन्हें सामूहिक रूप से चीनी भाषा कहा जाता है। चीन की प्रमुख और राष्ट्रव्यापी भाषा चीनी मन्दारिन है जो देश की आधिकारिक भाषा भी है। कुल मिलाकर चीन के ७५% लोग यह भाषा बोलते हैं। इसके अतिरिक्त यह ताइवान और सिंगापुर में भी आधिकारिक भाषा है। हांगकांग और मकाउ में कण्टोनी भाषा आधिकारिक है। इसके अतिरिक्त क्रमशः हांगकांग में अंग्रेज़ी और मकाउ में पुर्तगाली भाषाएँ भी आधिकारिक हैं। इसके अतिरिक्त चीन में बहुत सी भाषाएँ इसके नस्लीय समूहों द्वारा बोली जाती हैं जिन्हें झोंग्गुओ यूवेन कहा जाता है जिसका शाब्दिक अर्थ है "चीन की बोली और लेखन" जिसमें मुख्यतः छः भाषा परिवारों की भाषाएँ हैं।
